description: A choropleth map illustrating the spatial distribution of land cover and land use within Natura 2000 (N2K) sites across the European continent. The map depicts numerous small, irregularly shaped patches of colour, predominantly shades of green (ranging from yellowish-green to dark green) and some sparse light blue, overlaid onto a white background representing areas outside the depicted features. These patches outline the boundaries and internal characteristics of what are identified in the surrounding context as Natura 2000 sites. The green hues likely represent various natural and semi-natural land cover types such as forests, grasslands, and other vegetated areas, while the blue patches suggest the presence of water bodies or wetlands within these protected areas. The density of these sites appears higher in central Europe, along mountain ranges, and in parts of the Iberian Peninsula and Scandinavian countries. No legend, scale bar, compass orientation, or explicit reference year is provided in the image itself, however, the surrounding context indicates this data is from the Copernicus Land Monitoring Service (CLMS) Protected Areas product, providing detailed land cover/land use (LCLU) information for Natura 2000 sites.
